title: Morningstar Edu Assistant - onramp jot
content:
Call capture + immediate notes (raw, unedited)

Attendees: Jackson (Morningstar PM), Leila (platform lead), Samir (LMS admin), Ava, Diego
Time: 2025-02-11 10:30PT – ~45m

Goal: quick vet on feasibility for a hosted-first onramp for their student-facing assistant integrated into multiple LMS (Canvas primary, Blackboard second). Keep initial footprint hosted API, but requirements may push to Private/VPC for districts with FERPA concerns.

High-level asks from Morningstar
- Real-time Q&A assistant for students (short answers, reference links to course pages)
- Course content ingestion: weekly lecture notes + instructor-provided PDFs + discussion threads
- Per-course rate limits / per-instructor configs; billing visibility per org/team
- Single sign-on (SAML/Okta) + role mapping (student/TA/instructor)
- Audit logs / retention policies for compliance (must support 7 years for certain districts)

Quick feasibility notes (redwood perspective)
- Hosted API works for MVP: fast time-to-value, streaming responses, built-in rate limiting and per-token cost monitoring.
- FERPA-heavy districts will request Private w/ customer-managed keys. Need to surface the HSM/KMS flow and certs.
- Ingestion: we recommend batch embedding + incremental updates. Chunking strategy: 2–3 KB chunks with metadata (course_id, lecture_id, last_updated). Watch for PDF tokenization edge cases (scanned PDFs -> OCR -> bad tokens).
- Vector store: Morningstar prefers we host embeddings initially (Redwood Optimize + hosted vector store), but they asked about self-hosted vector DB later. Outline both: hosted (faster) vs dedicated (exportable snapshots).

Operational gotchas called out by Morningstar
- Burst traffic at assignment deadlines causes sudden spike — need autoscale + graceful fallback. Suggest model fallback policy: reduce to smaller model variant (e.g., from 16k to 8k quantized) for non-critical queries during spikes.
- Per-course quotas: they want enforcement at app-layer and token-level. Redwood per-token quotas + route-level throttles should work; need sample config to show how to map course -> route.
- PII in discussion posts: instructors sometimes paste student emails/IDs in posts. Must provide sanitization layer & retention deletion hooks. Legal wants proof of deletion.
- Cross-course embeddings leakage: be explicit about namespaceing vectors per course & version tags to avoid accidental exposure.

Prompting / UX notes
- Keep prompts short; rely on reranking for list answers. Provide canned system prompts per course type (quiz-style vs conceptual).
- Instructor override: allow adding course-specific prompt prefixes (admin UI) so TAs can tune tone.
- Citation policy: for any excerpt from course materials, return a source pointer (lecture id + timestamp). Need to design a structured output schema for the assistant to emit {answer, sources:[{type, id, snippet_loc}], confidence}.

Metrics to monitor (for pilot + SLOs)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 response time (aim p95 < 800ms for <512-token responses)
- Cost: cost per 1k tokens by route/model, and embedding update cost by course size
- Quality: hallucination incidents per 1k queries (via eval set + user feedback flag)
- Queueing: batch size and waiting time distribution (watch for long tail when prefixes cached)

Security / compliance items
- FERPA: some districts require on-prem or VPC. Roadmap: hosted -> Dedicated -> Private. Need checklist for entitlements and data residency.
- Key management: customer wants KMS integration and periodic rotation. Note: testing with Azure Key Vault + AWS KMS is common; include a short design doc.
- Audit logs: must capture request route, model version, prompt hash (not raw prompt) for privacy. Provide explanation of what we store and justify minimal retention.

Integration specifics & action items from call
- Diego: build a one-page sample mapping showing how course -> Redwood route config maps to quotas/role-based overrides. (Due: 2025-02-18)
- Ava: draft hosted vs private decision matrix + KMS integration notes + compliance checklist and share with Jackson. (Due: 2025-02-20)
- Priya: prototype ingestion pipeline doc for chunking and dedupe logic; include OCR fallback guidance for scanned PDFs. (Due: 2025-02-24)
- Jackson (Morningstar): will share a representative course bundle (10 lectures + 3 PDFs + discussion export) for an integration test. ETA: 2025-02-21

Follow-ups (short-term)
- Quick demo: set up a hosted test route with a small course vector index and an assistant prompt template. Show streaming and structured output. Aim to demo week of 2025-02-24.
- Security consult: schedule 1:1 with Redwood security to walk through FERPA checklist. Jackson wants a sample Data Processing Addendum.
- Eval harness: request a 50-sample question set from Morningstar to measure hallucination baseline.

Loose notes / brainstorm fragments
- Could offer per-course 'quiet hours' to throttle non-essential queries overnight to reduce cost.
- Consider "instructor-summarize" mode that uses longer context (8k window) to synthesize weekly summaries — may require dedicated capacity for predictable latency.
- If they go private, capture an onboarding runbook: network setup, cert exchange, bring-your-own-vector-store option.

Open questions (need answers from Morningstar)
1) Any districts already requiring on-prem? list please.
2) Expected concurrent students during peak finals week? (est. baseline needed for capacity planning)
3) Are there third-party copyrighted materials that instructors upload routinely? (copyright/policy implications)

Slack thread references: #edu-pilot-thread-cc-ava — contains raw export they sent (CSV of posts).

Next meeting: proposed 2025-02-25 10:00PT — demo + security checklist walk-through.

-- end of raw jot --

(Will tidy into a formal PRD once Morningstar confirms the sample bundle and we validate the prototype. This file intentionally rough.)
